item.title: North Carolina State football rumors: Philip Rivers smoke turning into fire
item.description: Kevin Ng-Imagn Images North Carolina State football rumors: Philip Rivers smoke turning into fire appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . North Carolina State lost to Stanford on the road on Saturday. After the game, NC State decided to move on from Dave Doren as the head coach. This is the first time since Tom O’Brien was fired in 2012 that the school is looking for a new head coach. One name that keeps popping up is former NC State quarterback Philip Rivers . Now, it seems those rumors are growing legs , according to Bruce Feldman of The Athletic. “‘It’s definitely more than smoke,’ an industry source told The Athletic on Sunday about the Rivers-to-NC State scenario,” Feldman wrote. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Rivers was the starting quarterback for NC State from 2000 through 2003. In his time there, he passed for 13,484 yards with 95 touchdowns while being named the ACC Player of the Year once. Since 2021, he has been the head coach of St. Michael Catholic. He is 50-19 as the head coach there. His son, Gunner Rivers, is the current quarterback for St. Michael Catholic and is comitted to NC State. “The 44-year-old Rivers, the ACC Player of the Year in 2003, interviewed last offseason for the Buffalo Bills head-coaching vacancy that went to Joe Brady. We heard the Bills brass was very impressed with Rivers and his vision. There are sure to be comparisons to former NFL QB Trent Dilfer’s jump from high school coach to FBS head coach at UAB, which did not go well. But as one NFL source noted to The Athletic, Rivers has a lot of ’emotional intelligence’ and basically called his own plays in the NFL,” Feldman added. The Dilfer era went just 9-21 at UAB before he was fired during the 2025 season. Prior to coaching at UAB, Dilfer had found success as the head coach of Lipcomb Academy. Still, there is one difference. Rivers was a much better quarterback than Dilfer. Now, whether he will be a better coach is yet to be seen. item.title: "We have to believe in ourselves" - Grifo reflects on late Freiburg fightback against Bayern
item.description: "We have to believe in ourselves" - Grifo reflects on late Freiburg fightback against Bayern SC Freiburg winger Vincenzo Grifo believes his side showed plenty of character in their late push against Bayern Munich, despite ultimately falling to a 3-1 defeat at the Europa-Park Stadion on Sunday evening. Julian Schuster's side found themselves two goals behind at the interval following strikes from Dayot Upamecano and Serge Gnabry, before a Tom Bischof own goal in the 82nd minute gave the hosts renewed hope. However, Bayern goalkeeper Jonas Urbig produced some important interventions to preserve the visitors' advantage, before Michael Olise sealed the victory in stoppage time. Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, Grifo acknowledged the quality of the opposition but insisted Freiburg had always believed they could find a way back into the contest. "Of course, Bayern have a lot of quality and allowed us relatively few chances in the first half," explained the veteran attacker. "That's FC Bayern. They have very, very high quality. "At half-time, we said that it could still be a dangerous scoreline, even for Bayern. If we score a goal, we'll have the fans and the stadium behind us again. "And then you could see that in the 80th or 81st minute, we were back in the game and perhaps had one or two opportunities." Grifo also offered an insight into Freiburg's tactical approach, explaining how their attempts to press Bayern high up the pitch left them vulnerable to counterattacks. "We wanted to go man-for-man today. Against Bayern, we wanted to press high and give their players as little space as possible. "But of course, there's always a risk. If you lose a duel, the opposition can suddenly have a clear run towards goal, as happened with the first goal. "We corrected that during the half-time team talk and tried to do things better. I think a lot more worked for us in the second half." While the Breisgau side come away from the weekend with nothing, Grifo was encouraged by Freiburg's determination in the closing stages, when they continued to threaten through set pieces. "We had another free-kick towards the end, three or four corners, and those situations can always be dangerous. "We told ourselves that we always have to believe in ourselves. We have that quality, and that's what we did. “Unfortunately, it wasn't enough in the end.”

item.description: O’Nien And Angulo Get 8 | Sunderland Players Rated In Scoreless Draw Vs Leeds United Sunderland welcomed Leeds United at the Stadium of Light earlier this evening as they hoped to secure a positive result at home in the Premier League. The Wearside club pushed on in search of the winning goal in the second 45 minutes but had to settle for a scoreless 0-0 draw in front of their home fans. Let’s take a look at how each Sunderland player fared during the clash against the Whites. GK: Robin Roefs – 7.5/10 He made a few solid saves at the back and did well to earn a clean sheet this evening. RB: Trai Hume – 6.5/10 Hume performed his defensive duties well and won a couple of aerial duels. CB: Nordi Mukiele – 7/10 He was a rock at the back and was good on the ball. Mukiele was replaced early in the second half. CB: Luke O’Nien – 8/10 O’Nien made a lot of crucial clearances at the back and did enough to secure a clean sheet. item.title: Sunderland stay bottom after home draw with Leeds
item.description: Sunderland stay bottom after home draw with Leeds Sunderland’s domestic struggles continued as they were held to a goalless draw by Leeds at the Stadium of Light. Whilst the Black Cats were more spirited in their performance, and ended a run of four straight Premier League defeats, they still lacked conviction in the final third. There was hope ahead of kick off that the returning Brian Brobbey would add potency to the Sunderland attack, but even he could not provide the difference for his side. Brobbey did come closer than anyone in the opening 45 to breaking the deadlock, but twice he was denied by James Trafford in the Leeds goal. For the most part though, the first half offered precious little for either side. Neither could find a meaningful rhythm, with the conditions playing their part in proceedings. Leeds had a short spell of pressure early in the second period, but it was Sunderland who began to test Trafford more often as the half wore on. He was at full stretch on several occasions in the space of a hectic ten-minute period as the home side pushed for the opener. There were cries from the stands for Chemsdine Talbi to be brought on from the bench, but even his eventual introduction could not muster up a goal for Sunderland. Leeds were perhaps disappointing by their own high standards this season, but will likely see this result as a point gained rather than two dropped. Certainly, they will not be as dissatisfied as Sunderland, who despite their efforts, remain rooted to the bottom of the Premier League table.

item.title: “Business as usual” – PSG coach refuses to give his players an excuse after triple blow
item.description: “Business as usual” – PSG coach refuses to give his players an excuse after triple blow PSG are missing some important players, but that’s not an excuse says manager Luis Enrique, who still expects the best. If you enjoy PSG Talk coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. PSG have been hit by a wave of injuries, with three first team stars coming off against Barcelona in midweek. But manager Luis Enrique isn’t going to let them use that as an excuse. In his press conference today he insisted that he still expected his team to be at the very top level, as they had been despite losing key players against Barca. Lucho promises “business as usual” after losing 3 players in one game Khcicha Kvaratshelia injured. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) “No, we’re not going to let up. We’re a family. There are 2-3 injured players, but that’s competition and the top level. You have to accept things. We’re the same team with and without the injuries,” the Spanish coach said. “That’s football. We played without Dembélé for almost the entire match against Barça, we played without Marquinhos and Kvara at the end. And we showed that we play the same way. That’s our strength. “It will be business as usual. I don’t want to change anything I’ve done, but I also want to change everything. That’s what you have to do to remain unpredictable. It depends on the team and the time of year. It’s true that losing 3 players in the same game is strange. It’s a motivation for us as a team. We’re moving on to improve.” In other news… Luis Enrique has denied PSG are going to sign a player in January to make up for the loss of Khvicha Kvarastkhelia. The PSG Barcelona game earlier this week broke TV records for a Champions League game in this phase.

item.description: Jonathan Taylor trade rumors: Ranking 4 landing spots for Colts RB from best to worst originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts are open to trading anyone before the Nov. 20 NFL trade deadline in the wake of dismissing GM Chris Ballard. That includes star running back Jonathan Taylor, their best offensive player. A combined report from ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport on Sunday named four notable suitors inquiring about acquiring Taylor. Those teams are the Green Bay Packers , Denver Broncos , Seattle Seahawks and Minnesota Vikings . The Vikings are the Colts' opponents for Week 7. The timing of the report is interesting. The Packers are getting back Josh Jacobs, while the Broncos are activating promising rookie Jonah Coleman. Likewise, Jordan Mason is healthy again for the Vikings. Zach Charbonnet was ruled out of his much-anticipated return for the Seahawks in Week 7, but has a good chance to play Week 8 vs. the Bears . Knowing that and looking at all four teams' overall backfield situations, here's the best and worst fit for Taylor. Denver Broncos The Broncos had high hopes for Coleman before the season, and he flashed some of it before hurting his ankle in Week 2 and landing on short-term injured reserve. JK Dobbins and RJ Harvey form the rest of the committee trying to support struggling Bo Nix with enough of a rushing attack plus reliable short-area receiving. Denver typically uses Dobbins to run and Harvey as a passing game outlet. Coleman offers a little juice in both areas. A trade for Taylor, however, would clean everything up with a clear three-down workhorse. The Broncos' run-blocking potential remains untapped, and Taylor can make it look a lot better. He could flip Denver's offense to being a lot more reliable under Sean Payton. 2. item.title: Howe It Happened: Steelers LB Payton Wilson Picks Off Saints, Finally Shows Coverage Potential
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Payton Wilson during a game against the Philadelphia Eagles on Dec. 15, 2024. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Pittsburgh Steelers’ defense stood firm on the ground against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. Tyler Shough posed much more of a problem to Mike McCarthy’s defense during the black and gold’s 16-10 win in Paris. Nearly halfway through the third quarter, the Saints’ quarterback was playing near-mistake-free behind center, having gone 22-for-27 for 212 yards and a one-yard touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele as the Saints drew closer to grabbing their first lead of the evening. Payton Wilson poured cold water on that idea, and made the Saints pay for dinking and dunking with a critical interception. “It took points off the board,” Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said afterward. “A big play. They were doing a very good job with the underneath completion game.” Wilson entered the day as the Steelers’ tackles leader, by a 14-stop margin. The 2024 third-round draft pick paced the team in takedowns last season, too, and before that campaign proclaimed himself as “one of the better cover linebackers in the world.” He then posted a 104.3 passer rating allowed, per Pro Football Focus . No. 41 now has another point to his argument. item.title: After missing Australia tour, fresh injury setback rules Nahid Rana out of West Indies series
item.description: Bangladesh fast bowler Nahid Rana is set to miss the upcoming two-Test series against West Indies after being diagnosed with a labrum tear. The injury has also raised doubts over his availability for Bangladesh's two-Test tour of South Africa in November. The pacer was initially believed to be suffering from weakness in his back and pelvic area, but the board decided to send him overseas for a second opinion. Rana was left out of Bangladesh's 15-member squad for the first Test against West Indies in Mirpur, announced on Friday. He is now expected to miss the entire two-match series. “Yes, a labrum tear has been detected,” a BCB official was quoted as saying by Cricbuzz. “He has already been given an injection in Australia and he has started his rehabilitation program. He is likely to bowl on Friday (October 30)." The latest injury is another setback for Rana, who had been working towards a return after suffering a grade-two side strain during Bangladesh's tour of Zimbabwe in July. That injury ruled him out of the tour of Australia, the Asian Games and the one-off Test against Afghanistan. Rana then suffered a fresh glute injury during his rehabilitation, which forced him to miss the tri-series in the UAE involving Afghanistan and Zimbabwe. Bangladesh will host West Indies in a two-Test series beginning on October 28 before travelling to South Africa for a tour comprising two Tests, three ODIs and three T20Is. The South Africa tour is scheduled to begin on November 15.

item.title: Russia to host first sporting World Championships since invasion of Ukraine
item.description: Moscow will host the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships, marking the first time Russia will host any world championships in an Olympic sport since it invaded Ukraine in 2022. The International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) announced its decision on Sunday, with Ahmedabad in India awarded the 2029 edition at the same time. Russia’s status as a pariah state in the sporting world is slowly coming to an end, with Russian and Belarusian weightlifters eligible to compete in IWF events since the International Olympic Committee provisionally lifted its suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee in July. The IOC Executive Board, when it lifted the suspension, said athletes should not be held responsible for the actions of their governments. No decision has yet been ⁠taken on whether Russian athletes will compete under their national flag, colours and anthem at the Olympic Games. The National Olympic Committee of Ukraine has appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport against the IOC's decision. The ROC was suspended in October 2023 after recognising regional Olympic councils in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian territories of Luhansk, Donetsk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia, following Russia's ‌invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. The 2025 World Aquatics Championships were originally awarded to the Russian city of Kazan but were later moved to Singapore. This will be the first time since 1983 that Moscow has hosted the World Weightlifting Championships. “All the bids we received were excellent and we are sure that the Championships in ⁠your respective countries will be a huge success," said IWF General ​Secretary ⁠Jose Quinones. Russia's return to international competition also comes against the backdrop of one of the biggest doping scandals in Olympic sport. The country ⁠has been under scrutiny since a 2015 World Anti-Doping Agency -commissioned report ⁠found evidence of systematic doping in Russian athletics, while subsequent investigations uncovered a state-backed cover-up ‌linked to the ​2014 Sochi Winter Olympics. The IOC said all Russian athletes now returning to international competition would have to meet relevant anti-doping requirements. Additional reporting by Reuters

item.title: Sage responds to questions over his Crystal Palace future after loss to Newcastle
item.description: Sage responds to questions over his Crystal Palace future after loss to Newcastle Pierre Sage says he believes he still has the backing of Crystal Palace’s hierarchy despite the growing pressure following a 2-0 defeat to Newcastle United. Palace have picked up just seven points from their first eight league games. Asked whether he feels he has the support of those running the club, Sage replied: “I think, yeah. “The question is, do you think? And my reply is, yes, I think.” Palace were booed by sections of the support after another disappointing result, but Sage insisted his focus remains on the players rather than the noise surrounding his position. “It’s normal that a person loses patience when you lose, because everybody wants to win, and us first,” Sage said. “We want to win, we do the job to win, but today it was not the case, in this period it was not the case. “I don’t have to convince the people around the club, I just have to convince the players to do their best and to compete and to continue their improvement. “After that, this kind of decision of what we are talking about is to the chairman, to the owners, this kind of person. “For me, the noise around the team, the noise around the club, it’s only noise.” Reflecting on the defeat, Sage felt Palace were punished for a short period in which their level dropped. “A game of football is imperfect, because there’s a lot of mistakes,” he said. “Every player makes mistakes, every coach makes decisions that are not in line with what we need these days. “And it’s always a frustration to not achieve the perfect things. “In our period, we have to be perfect to win, and today we missed 15 minutes. “In my position, I just have to create the conditions to be close to perfection with the team, in concentration, in play, in the way of defending, in the way of attacking. “But today we missed only 15 minutes, but it’s sufficient for our opponent to win.”

item.title: Pressure grows on Sage as fans turn on Palace boss
item.description: "Oliver Glasner achieved some amazing things, and now I have to do the same," Pierre Sage said after replacing the man who delivered an FA Cup, European trophy and Community Shield during two years in charge at Selhurst Park. Four months into a three-year contract, the Frenchman is already under big pressure after a fifth defeat in eight Premier League games left the Eagles in the bottom four. Palace have failed to win their past four games and Sunday's 2-0 home defeat by Newcastle was greeted with boos from home fans, who had turned up hoping to see a positive response after last weekend's 5-0 humiliation at fierce rivals Brighton. "There is no noise inside the club," said Sage when asked about his future in his post-match media conference. "The boos are normal because we don't have the result. "The noise is the consequence of the result of the team, and at the moment we don't have what we expect. "Inside, we are just really focused on solutions. How to be better, how to create the conditions to compete, and we will continue our work, and there's no noise inside." Asked about boos from home fans during the match and at full-time, Sage accepted it was an expected response after failing to win. "It's normal that people lose patience when you lose, because everybody wants to win. Today it was not the case." Sage was named Ligue 1 manager of the year after leading Lens to a second-place finish as well as a French Cup triumph. But could time already be running out for the 47-year-old? Sage 'too nice at times' Sage struck a defiant tone during his post-match media conference as he addressed questions about his future for 20 minutes. "I don't have to convince the people around the club. I just have to convince the players to do their best to compete and to continue to improve," he added when asked further about his job. "After that, this kind of decision is for the chairman, to the owners, this kind of person. "For me, the noise around the team, the noise around the club, it's only noise." Palace have just seven points from their first eight league games in the post-Glasner era. After losing to Everton and Manchester City in their first two matches, Palace won at Fulham before losing at home to newly promoted Ipswich. They secured a rare clean sheet in a goalless draw at Leeds before coming from behind to beat Nottingham Forest at Selhurst Park on 11 October. That was their last win. They have since lost at his former club Lyon in the Europa League, and Brighton, before drawing 2-2 against Besiktas in Istanbul on Thursday. However, patience is clearly wearing thin after fans reacted to the latest defeat by Newcastle. In addition, Palace have the worst defensive record in the Premier League after conceding 19 goals in eight games. Their next Premier League match is at improving Tottenham next Saturday, before hosting Liverpool on 8 November going into the international break. Palace's first game back is at fellow strugglers Coventry City on 21 November.

item.description: Live La Liga updates, kick-off 8pm (GMT) Sid Lowe: Mourinho’s Madrid primed for battle Live scoreboard | And you can email Niall We’ll have full team news shortly, but Real Madrid keeper Thibaut Courtois has already been ruled out of tonight’s game due to illness. “Courtois is a last-minute withdrawal (from the squad) due to a bout of the flu,” Madrid said in a statement. item.title: ‘That Was the Goal’: Steelers Knew They Could Run All Over Saints
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) hands off to running back Jaylen Warren (30) against the New Orleans Saints during the first quarter at Stade de France Stadium on Oct. 25, 2026. -- Kirby Lee / Imagn Images IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Pittsburgh Steelers had their way with the New Orleans Saints on the ground in Sunday’s 16-10 win in Paris. Pittsburgh rushed for 148 yards on 30 carries, an average of 4.9 yards per carry. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said in his postgame press conference that imposing their will on the Saints was the goal. The Saints came into Sunday’s game with the 30th-ranked run defense. The Steelers also smashed the run on defense, allowing only 18 yards on 17 attempts (1.1 average). “We felt as a football team that we needed to own the line of scrimmage on both sides,” McCarthy told reporters. “We felt going through the game plan process, that was gonna be an important factor in the game and we definitely hit the target there, we were able to get up to 30 rushes. That was the goal to get the rush attempts up.” Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers echoed his head coach’s statement. “I felt like we controlled the line of scrimmage with Jaylen [Warren] and Rico [Dowdle]” Rodgers said. “I thought Rico had a nice week last week, another nice week this week. We’re not going to get numb to it, but we’re almost expecting Jaylen to have 100 yards and make some splash plays. He’s just so dynamic, so love those guys. We knew coming in, we could run against them.” Jaylen Warren rushed for 101 yards on 18 carries (5.6 average). He also had three receptions for 36 yards. Rico Dowdle rushed for 41 yards on nine carries (4.6 average). Through the air, he had six receptions for 45 yards. “We knew what we knew about them. So we wanted to, you know, use our strength against their weaknesses,” Warren said. The Steelers certainly have a dynamic duo with Warren and Dowdle. The offensive line is also starting to really blossom. “I think anytime we can just line up and give you Jaylen and Rico all day, that’s a good day for us,” McCarthy said. item.title: “I already said…” – Luis Enrique makes his stance on January transfers clear
item.description: “I already said…” – Luis Enrique makes his stance on January transfers clear PSG are equipped with enough players in attack to survive the absence of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, says Luis Enrique. If you enjoy PSG Talk coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. PSG are preparing to take on Lyon in an interesting Monday night game in Ligue 1, but in his press conference previewing the game there were more questions about the injuries his team picked up in the Champions League game against Barcelona on Tuesday than there were about the game ahead. PSG prepared for season without key attacker claims coach Luis Enrique’s press conference. Luis Enrique was of course asked if his team would consider making new signings, especially in attack where they’ve lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for the season. He insisted that wasn’t on his agenda: “No injury justifies signing new players. I already said at the start of the season that we could manage two or three significant injuries that lead to absences,” the Spanish coach said. “But it’s clear that we remain attentive to every possibility of recruiting a new player if we think we really need one. We always have this responsibility to be attentive to opportunities during the transfer window. But not to compensate for an injury.” Ferran Torres will now be a fixture in the starting team, with Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts also expected to soak up some extra minutes. In other news… The PSG Barcelona game earlier this week broke TV records for a Champions League game in this phase. Despite his injury, PSG want to secure Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a new contract sooner rather than later. Desire Doue has received a first verbal offer from PSG over a new contract, and could sign his new deal before too long.

item.title: Bayern pass test of courage after Kompany shock with 3-1 in Freiburg
item.description: Bayern Munich's Dayot Upamecano celebrates scoring his side's first goal during the German Bundesliga soccer match between SC Freiburg and Bayern Munich at Europa-Park Stadium. (is associated with: «Bayern pass test of courage after Kompany shock with 3-1 in Freiburg») Harry Langer/dpa Bayern Munich overcame the collapse of coach Vincent Kompany and the additional absence of key players with a 3-1 triumph at Freiburg on Sunday and returned to the top of the Bundesliga. Dayot Upamecano opened the scoring in the 16th minute when he blocked a shot from Niklas Beste at his own penalty area, ran on to get the ball back from Michael Olise at the centre circle and one-on-one fired a low shot past Mio Backhaus. Serge Gnabry scored the second in the 42nd into the far corner off a through-ball from Nathaniel Brown for his 100th Bundesliga goal. Bayern were the much better team but an own goal from Tom Bischof in the 82nd made them sweat it out in the final minutes, and they needed a huge save from Jonas Urbig in stoppage time against Matthias Ginter before Olise clinched it at the death when he stole the ball from until then superb goalkeeper Backhaus. Bayern passed a big test of courage two days after Kompany collapsed at their training centre and assistant Aaron Danks took charge for the time being. The Dallas Cowboys have officially named their Thanksgiving Day game halftime show performer. Country music star Miranda Lambert will be hitting the stage at halftime when the Cowboys host the Philadelphia Eagles on Nov. 26 at 4:30 pm ET. “There’s something special about how music brings people together, especially when it’s to spread joy and hope to families who need it most,” Lambert said in a press release. “The Salvation Army and the Dallas Cowboys have built an incredible tradition with the Red Kettle Kickoff, and I can’t wait to be back home in Texas this Thanksgiving to help carry it forward.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Thanksgiving Day halftime show is more than just a break for fans but also marks the 30th anniversary of the show, putting a spotlight on benefiting The Salvation Army and the Red Kittle Campaign, which runs through Christmas Eve. This year will be the organization’s 136 th Red Kettle Campaign, where every dollar donated stays local to fund year-round social services, including food pantries, shelter, utility assistance, and holiday meals. “The Red Kettle Kickoff has become one of the Dallas Cowboys’ proudest traditions and one that my family and our entire organization look forward to every Thanksgiving,” said Charlotte Jones, chief brand officer and co-owner of the Dallas Cowboys, and former national advisory board chairman for The Salvation Army. “For 30 years, incredible artists have taken our halftime stage to help The Salvation Army bring hope to millions of people in need. We’re grateful to Miranda Lambert for joining that legacy and helping us continue this meaningful tradition.” Last year, Post Malone was the Cowboys’ Thanksgiving Day halftime show performer. Other Thanksgiving Day games are the Chicago Bears at Detroit Lions and Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills. Before the Thanksgiving Day matchup, the Cowboys and Eagles will face off on Monday, October 26, at 8:15 pm ET. Carrick's bold decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes backfired as defeat stretched United's winless run to eight games and left them 16th in the Premier League, just one point above the relegation zone. For the third time in four seasons, the Cherries won by a three-goal margin at Old Trafford as strikes from Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson secured a fully deserved victory for Marco Rose's side. Fernandes was critical of Carrick's tactics in a 4-1 Champions League thrashing at Como on Wednesday. The United boss said the decision to leave out last season's Premier League Player of the Year was "purely football" driven, but it was hard to believe Fernandes was not being punished as he was left on the bench for the entire match. Carrick was taunted with chants of "you're getting sacked in the morning" from the Bournemouth fans. But on this evidence, dismissing another manager is far from a quick fix for a club that has fallen dramatically from grace since Alex Ferguson's retirement after winning their most recent English title 13 years ago. item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

Nothing erudite, anyway. item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
